device.name: Sensirion SHT31 Smart Gadget (Smart Humigadget)
device.notes:
A connected-only legacy temperature/humidity design advertising the exact name Smart Humigadget. Live values are four-byte little-endian IEEE-754 binary32 numbers on separate humidity and temperature characteristics. The same two characteristics later multiplex history packets with a four-byte sequence prefix, so packet length is mandatory when decoding.
Do NOT assign the newer company-0x06D5 passive type 00 04 format, the tick-based conversions, or the newer 00008000-… logger to this device. Sensirion's current protocol page explicitly excludes Smart Humigadget from that logger. Its current humidity row also says uint8, but the official legacy firmware sends a four-byte float; the firmware is the generation-specific authority here.
The legacy f234 logger uses uint64 little-endian epoch milliseconds for synchronization/range values and a uint32 little-endian interval in milliseconds. History floats contain no per-value timestamp. Each stream is newest-first, and timestamps are reconstructed from the selected newest time, interval, sequence number, and value position.

openness.notes: The vendor published the complete legacy firmware and profile. This spec follows that generation, not the newer Arduino manufacturer-sample protocol or its 00008000-… logger.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The more-than-one-second button press enables advertising; it is not a separate authenticated pairing mode and supplies no PIN.

exclusivity.recovery: Disconnect the existing central and reconnect. If Bluetooth was disabled, hold the board button for more than one second to enable it; there is no stored bond to forget or clear.

pairing.notes: The user guide says 'pair' in the ordinary connect-to-a-phone sense, but the official firmware exposes unencrypted GATT read/write/notify properties and defines no PIN/bonding workflow. This is a source-derived no-link-layer-pairing answer, not a hardware security audit.

unpair.clears: Not applicable: the documented firmware does not create a persistent bond.
unpair.notes: Disconnecting ends the link but does not erase logged measurements.

credentials.notes: No Wi-Fi passphrase, account token, application key, or persistent BLE bond is used by the documented legacy firmware.

factory_reset.description: Do not represent the Bluetooth toggle, battery removal, or logger interval change as a verified full reset. No candidate reset procedure is published here.
factory_reset.effect: No full factory-reset procedure or bond-clearing effect is established. The documented long button press toggles Bluetooth only; an interval write clears history but is not a factory reset.

methods.description: Enable Bluetooth on the board, scan for Smart Humigadget, connect, and subscribe to the two measurement characteristics.

steps.action: With the board powered, hold its switch button for more than one second to enable Bluetooth.
steps.expect: The Bluetooth symbol blinks and the device ID appears briefly; the board advertises as Smart Humigadget.

steps.action: Scan for the exact name Smart Humigadget and connect over GATT without requesting a bond.
steps.expect: The Bluetooth symbol becomes steady while connected.

steps.action: Subscribe to 00001235-… and 00002235-… and decode exactly four-byte notifications as live float32 values.
steps.expect: Relative humidity in percent and temperature in degrees Celsius arrive independently.

setup.notes: There is no credential provisioning. The user enables the radio with the onboard button, then a client connects directly. Confidence is medium: the procedure is in the official user guide and firmware, unreplayed here.

rejoin.notes: The board joins no Wi-Fi network and the documented firmware keeps no client bond. Disconnect the previous central, enable Bluetooth with the button if needed, and connect from the new phone. Download history before changing its interval.

testing.notes: No physical scan, connection, live notification, clock sync, history download, interval write, or reset was performed for this spec on 2026-11-11. Official legacy firmware/profile/app source and the vendor user guide supply the reported behavior. Independent tests use invented float, history, and timestamp packets only.

evidence.documentation_review: Reviewed 2026-11-11: official SHT31 user guide, Smart Gadget profile, legacy firmware commit 0fca4bb7, and official Android app commit f1bfb86b. All byte-level behavior is reported from source; no hardware verification was performed. Current cross-family documentation was used only to record the explicit Smart Humigadget exclusion and the conflicting humidity type.
evidence.open_questions: Actual packet captures and timestamp alignment, maximum simultaneous centrals, behavior of zero/invalid floats, completion timing tolerance, battery-cycle effects, and a full reset/recovery procedure still need hardware. No firmware-update interface is asserted.

LegacyHistoryPacket.description: One history notification on either legacy measurement characteristic during an f234 download.

fields.description: Bytes 0-3: uint32 LE one-based position of values[0] in this service's download order; not a timestamp.
fields.name: sequence

fields.description: One to four consecutive float32 LE measurements. Unit comes from the characteristic: percent RH or degrees Celsius.
fields.name: values

parse_rules: Accept only lengths 8, 12, 16, or 20. The value count is (length - 4) / 4; exactly 4 bytes is a live measurement instead.
Maintain sequence state independently for humidity and temperature. The first history packet for each has sequence 1.
Within and across packets, values run newest to oldest. For zero-based value slot j in a packet, timestamp_ms = selected_newest_epoch_ms - (sequence - 1 + j) * logger_interval_ms.
selected_newest_epoch_ms is the read-back 0000f237-… range end after synchronization and any optional narrowing. All timestamps and the interval are milliseconds, not seconds.
Do not mistake interleaved four-byte live values for history, or a zero completion notification on 0000f238-… for another measurement.

LegacyLiveMeasurement.description: One live humidity or temperature notification/read on the legacy measurement characteristics.

fields.description: Exactly four bytes: IEEE-754 binary32 little-endian. Percent RH on 00001235-…, degrees Celsius on 00002235-….
fields.name: value

parse_rules: Accept exactly 4 bytes and decode with a little-endian binary32 operation (for example Python struct '<f').
Do not apply the newer 16-bit tick transfer functions, and do not decode a longer history packet with this rule.

LegacyTimestamp.description: The eight-byte values used by f235/f236/f237.

fields.description: Unsigned 64-bit little-endian Unix epoch milliseconds; 64 bits are required, so a 32-bit decoder is insufficient.
fields.name: epoch_ms

parse_rules: Read or write exactly 8 bytes and decode as uint64 little-endian.
Do not confuse these absolute epoch-millisecond values with the logger's internal uptime counters or a history sequence number.

protocol_details.generation: Legacy SHT31 Smart Gadget firmware, not newer Arduino BLE Gadget protocol
logger_flow: Write current Unix epoch milliseconds to 0000f235-… as uint64 LE, then read the computed 0000f236-… and 0000f237-… range values.
Optionally narrow the range with eight-byte writes to f236/f237; these writes change selection, not stored data.
Subscribe to 00001235-…, 00002235-…, and 0000f238-… before writing 01 to f238.
Classify every measurement notification by exact length, maintain independent channel sequences, and reconstruct timestamps from the selected newest range end.
Finish when f238 notifies zero; disconnecting cancels. Do not issue another sync or interval write mid-download.
protocol_details.manufacturer_samples: Not documented or claimed for this device; company 0x06D5 type 00 04 belongs to the newer family spec.

start_write.live_side_effect: Four-byte live values can interleave at reduced cadence during download
start_write.trigger: any nonzero value; 01 is the published conventional trigger

test_vectors.provenance: All packets and timestamps are invented; no unit ID, address, serial, or owner data is present.

remaining_unknowns: No hardware flow was run; the independent tests prove only that the documented packets and arithmetic are mutually consistent.
Read-back range quantization and per-sample timestamps should be compared with a physical download before treating absolute times as calibrated.
Single-central behavior, invalid/sentinel float handling, power-cycle persistence, and exact completion timing are not established.
No full factory reset, unpairing procedure, OTA/DFU entry, image format, or interrupted-update recovery is documented; no DFU feature is declared.

format.name: relative_humidity_percent
format.notes: LIVE PACKETS ONLY, exactly four bytes. Route 8/12/16/20-byte values through payload_formats.LegacyHistoryPacket instead.

characteristics.name: Relative Humidity / History
characteristics.notes: Live: 4-byte float32 LE percent RH. History during an f234 download: uint32 LE sequence followed by one to four float32 LE RH values, yielding exactly 8, 12, 16, or 20 bytes. Sequence starts at 1 and identifies the first value in download order; it is not a timestamp.

services.name: Relative Humidity (legacy)
services.notes: Live and history share 00001235-…. Exactly four bytes means live; 8/12/16/20 bytes means history. The current cross-family web table's uint8 label does not describe this official legacy firmware.

format.name: temperature_c
format.notes: LIVE PACKETS ONLY, exactly four bytes. Route 8/12/16/20-byte values through payload_formats.LegacyHistoryPacket instead.

characteristics.name: Temperature / History
characteristics.notes: Live: 4-byte float32 LE degrees Celsius. History: uint32 LE sequence plus one to four float32 LE temperature values, exactly 8/12/16/20 bytes. Temperature and humidity have independent streams/sequences.

services.name: Temperature (legacy)
services.notes: Live and history share 00002235-… and use the same length discriminator as humidity.

synchronize_clock.description: Write the client's current Unix epoch time as exactly eight uint64-le bytes; this selects the initial full-history range without erasing samples.

epoch_ms_le.description: Current Unix epoch milliseconds encoded as one unsigned 64-bit little-endian integer; do not send seconds, ASCII, or a 32-bit value.

characteristics.name: Synchronize Time
characteristics.notes: Exactly eight bytes: uint64 little-endian Unix epoch milliseconds. Writing establishes the current logging grid and causes the device to calculate readable newest/oldest range values and the initial download count. Synchronize again after every interval change.

set_oldest_requested_time.description: Optionally move the requested range start to an eight-byte epoch-millisecond value before starting; firmware clamps/rounds it and does not erase samples.

oldest_epoch_ms_le.description: Requested oldest timestamp as uint64 little-endian Unix epoch milliseconds.

format.name: oldest_epoch_ms_le
format.notes: Decode as uint64 little-endian Unix epoch milliseconds; schema format has no uint64 type.

characteristics.name: Oldest Sample Time / Range Start
characteristics.notes: Eight-byte uint64 little-endian epoch milliseconds. After sync, read the computed lower bound. An optional write narrows the next download; firmware clamps it to the available range and rounds the start upward to the logging grid. This does not delete history.

set_newest_requested_time.description: Optionally move the requested range end to an eight-byte epoch-millisecond value before starting; firmware clamps/rounds it and does not erase samples.

newest_epoch_ms_le.description: Requested newest timestamp as uint64 little-endian Unix epoch milliseconds.

format.name: newest_epoch_ms_le
format.notes: Decode as uint64 little-endian Unix epoch milliseconds; schema format has no uint64 type.

characteristics.name: Newest Sample Time / Range End
characteristics.notes: Eight-byte uint64 little-endian epoch milliseconds. This selected newest value anchors per-value timestamps. An optional write narrows the range; firmware clamps it and rounds downward to the logging grid. Do not infer a packet timestamp from the sequence prefix.

start_history_download.description: Start the prepared newest-first history transfer after synchronization/range selection and after subscribing to humidity, temperature, and this completion characteristic.

characteristics.name: Start Download / Completion
characteristics.notes: Any nonzero one-byte write starts the prepared download; 01 is the conventional trigger. A write while already active has no additional effect. History then appears on 00001235-… and 00002235-…, not on this characteristic. Live four-byte values can still interleave at a reduced cadence. Device completion is a zero-valued notification on this characteristic, emitted after a short delay. Disconnect cancels.

set_logger_interval_ms.advanced_reason: Every interval write permanently clears all onboard temperature and humidity history and resets the time base. Download wanted history first, then synchronize the clock again.
set_logger_interval_ms.description: Set the logging interval in milliseconds; the device normalizes to at least 1000 ms in whole-second steps and erases all history.

interval_ms.description: Requested milliseconds. Firmware rounds down to a multiple of 1000 and substitutes 1000 when the rounded result is zero; read back the accepted interval.

characteristics.name: Logger Interval
characteristics.notes: uint32 little-endian milliseconds; default 600000 ms (10 minutes). A write rounds down to a whole-second boundary, with 0..999 ms and zero normalized to 1000 ms. EVERY WRITE clears all logged values and resets the firmware's internal time and synchronization counters. Download wanted history first, then synchronize again before use.

services.name: Legacy Logger
services.notes: Legacy only; not interchangeable with 00008000-…. Before downloading, synchronize epoch time, read the resulting range, subscribe to both measurement streams and to the completion characteristic, then write a nonzero byte to 0000f238-…. Disconnect cancels an active download.
